caveats: The Nov 5 launch is on Microsoft Tech Community, not the Foundry devblog. The local devblog clone did not contain this announcement.
Microsoft Learn's fal services notice says processing is outside Microsoft facilities and the Microsoft customer agreements, DPA, and certifications do not apply.
The launch says US-hosted; Learn specifies US Data Zone for Kling and Global Standard PayGo for LTX/MiniMax. This does not establish all Azure US regions as deployable.
No matching fal catalog entries were observed in East US or East US 2 while the feature was unregistered. This is not proof of global unavailability.
No matching fal quota entries were returned in East US 2. Effective subscription RPM remains unverified; documented tiers are 0, 2, or 40 RPM.

The launch pricing prose says per minute but its table heading says per video second. Pricing evidence and illustrative calculations are retained in evidence.json and README notes only; no prices appear in the on-screen visual. Confirm the unit before use.
No measured speed, quality, fps, file size, or generated sample exists. Do not present this infographic as a model output or benchmark.
Runner defaults to an available speed-oriented configured model, not an empirically fastest model. Versioned API routes follow Learn examples but live integration is unverified.
No Azure resources or deployments were created, and no third-party terms were accepted.
